text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois should be on high alert for active law enforcement, government imposter, and home repair scams reported by local sheriffs and the state attorney general.
snippet_highlighted_words: active law enforcement, government imposter, and home repair scams

list.snippet: Jail and Bond Scams: Scammers are contacting family members of inmates, claiming money or gift cards are needed to secure a loved one's release from jail. Authorities emphasize that these are fraudulent and note that Illinois has ended cash bail, meaning legitimate bond payments are never handled this way.

Fake Arrest Warrants and Police Imposters: Scammers spoof phone numbers or send texts pretending to be from local sheriff's offices (such as in Macon County , McLean County , and Lee County ) or federal prosecutors in the Central District of Illinois . They claim victims missed jury duty or have warrants, demanding immediate payment via Bitcoin, gift cards, or cash.

DMV and State Police Text Scams: Fraudulent texts mimicking the Secretary of State, Department of Transportation, or State Police claim recipients have unpaid traffic violations or vehicle infractions, threatening license suspension if a payment link is clicked.

Home Improvement and Construction Fraud: Consistently ranked as a top complaint by the Attorney General's office, dishonest contractors solicit door-to-door in local neighborhoods, take large upfront down payments for roof or paving repairs, and never complete the work.
Verify independently: Real law enforcement and government agencies will never call or text demanding immediate payment, Bitcoin, gift cards, or wire transfers.
Do not click links: Never interact with or click payment links in unsolicited text messages regarding traffic fines or warrants.
File a complaint: Report suspected fraud to the Office of the Illinois Attorney General or contact your local county sheriff’s department.
